A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CitePretrain with matching research identity, method and benchmark. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting and added analyses.

before.justification: v2 reports original four-benchmark evaluations, scaling and memorization experiments, hybrid citation comparisons, and additional empirical studies in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds model evaluations, title-shortcut analysis, hybrid conflict analysis and out-of-domain experiments.

M1.justification: The two-stage training procedure, forward and backward augmentation, title-constrained decoding and hybrid inference procedures remain unchanged. Sections 3–4 and the corresponding implementation and augmentation appendices document the same method.

E1.justification: The original corpora and QA benchmarks are retained. Appendix B.4 adds an out-of-domain scenario: held-out Wikipedia/arXiv language modeling and TriviaQA transfer after RepliQA-only continual pretraining. This extends task requirements within already represented domains.

E2.justification: The main comparator set remains unchanged. The new OOD comparison in Table 6 includes raw-text pretraining without identifiers and integer-ID controls alongside no-pretraining, title-ID and repeated-title variants. v2 did not evaluate this comparator set for OOD effects.

E3.justification: v3 extends the main evaluation to Qwen-2.5-14B, Llama-3.2-3B and Llama-3.1-8B. It also introduces title-rank bins, correctness-based conflict slices, augmentation-fraction comparisons and token-matched OOD controls with perplexity and transfer accuracy. These substantially expand evaluation design; existing main training settings and splits are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's existing scaling, memorization, identifier and qualitative analyses, v3 adds quantitative title-shortcut testing (Table 2), forward/backward scaling comparisons (Figure 4), hybrid conflict analysis (Table 5) and OOD forgetting analysis (Table 6). These address several additional diagnostic questions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance-testing procedures. The added results continue the existing practice of reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Original Table 1, v2 Tables 2–4 (v3 Tables 3, 7 and 8), and Figures 2–3 retain their results. Substantial new entries include additional model results, 40.0% citation precision in the Very Hard title bin, conflict-slice accuracies and OOD outcomes. Table 6 reports Wikipedia perplexity of 26.52 for Active Indexing versus 6.71 for the base model; these are newly evaluated conditions.

T1.justification: The corpus, answer and augmentation definitions remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version provides theoretical proofs or theorems, and v3 adds no formal derivation or assumption. Its title-rank diagnostic is an empirical evaluation procedure.

C1.justification: The benchmark and method contributions, headline citation gains and conclusion's main findings are retained. The introduction adds an explicit claim of greater token efficiency than rephrasing-only methods and attributes continued scaling to combinatorial cross-document synthesis.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations about learning beyond title shortcuts, hybrid arbitration and the relationship between forgetting, perplexity and knowledge retention. Some interpretations conflict with the evidence: Appendix B.3 describes 58.2 accuracy as improving over Internal-only, although Table 5 gives that baseline 100.0 in the same slice. The original limitations are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: v2 promises code and data upon publication; v3 reports their release and supplies a repository address. v3 also expands title-processing documentation and specifies new analysis budgets, including 66M forward and 76M backward tokens in Appendix B.2. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware, timings and prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chen et al. (2025), Villalobos et al. (2024), Muennighoff et al. (2023) and Qin et al. (2025), supporting citation complementarity and the synthetic-data motivation. Existing positioning against retrieval-based and source-aware approaches is largely retained. Duplicate bibliography entries are consolidated without removing the underlying works.

P1.justification: There are focused rewrites of the motivation, dataset explanation and model-scaling discussion, plus acknowledgments and a new Additional Results appendix. Most existing prose and section order remain intact; subsequent appendices are relabeled rather than substantively reorganized.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 2 and 4–6 and Figure 4; Table 4 partly redisplays existing results. Table 1 combines the separate model blocks under explicit Model/Method columns. The conference format changes typography, headers, abstract layout and placement throughout, including relocation of the unchanged Figure 3.

improvement.justification: v3 adds quantitative checks of title shortcuts and OOD side effects absent from v2, broader backbone validation, and a reported code/data release. These improve empirical scrutiny and reproducibility information. However, new interpretation errors limit the gain: Appendix B.3 calls 58.2 accuracy an improvement over a 100.0 baseline, and B.4 misstates Table 6's perplexity ordering. The additional evidence remains useful, while the main method and original findings stay stable.
